name: Garden Egg Leaf Spot
description: A fungal leaf disease that causes circular brown spots with target-like concentric rings on garden egg leaves. It reduces photosynthetic area and causes premature leaf drop, leading to smaller fruits and lower yields.
symptoms: Small circular brown spots with concentric rings
Spots enlarge and merge forming large dead areas
Lower leaves affected first, then spreading upward
Severely affected leaves turn yellow and drop
Fruits may develop sunken spots near the stem end
causes: Fungal spores from infected plant debris
Prolonged leaf wetness from rain or overhead irrigation
Poor air circulation from dense planting
treatments: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves
Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil at 7-10 day intervals
Apply neem oil solution (5ml/L water) as organic treatment
prevention: Space plants adequately for good airflow
Water at the base of plants, avoid wetting leaves
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash
Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
